🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 9)
Channel: alert-system (+ blast radius in alert-no-code-next-gen)  •  bug-type guess: data/code  •  alerts in group: ~174
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`) — owns App Install/Update. Also `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`) for the Sales Orders app content, `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`) for ms-tables-fields-api.

*Root cause:* a single template-app push. At *13:13:13.53Z* `app-update-agent` logged `App Publish - Started - Push Update [App: "Sales Orders", AppId: 55b7fa26-9d45-400d-829f-a3610098567c, Version: 182, JobId: d055f8dd-9bb5-4996-9d71-dd7bae39c557, Publisher: "templatedevv2"]`. The first bundle failure lands *3.7s later* (13:13:17.21Z). Everything else this morning is downstream of that one event.

Symptoms:
  - *196 accounts failed* the update. 179 × HTTP 400 / ErrorCode 50 — `The field 'Name' already exists` on view `InvSalesOrderRevertReason`; +15 "data misaligned" (`Can not add field Job of Type Text to SalesOrder because source type is DropDown`). Deterministic validation rejections, not timeouts.
  - *Partial schema left behind (the serious bit).* The bundle is NOT atomic. The API response shows `SuccessfulBundle`=[`viewPreferencesMethod` → `DefaultInvSalesOrderRevertReason` *created*] while `UnSuccessfulBundle`=[`InvSalesOrderRevertReason` *failed*]. Those 196 accounts now have a preference pointing at a table that does not exist, with no rollback. *Re-running the push will not fix them — it hits the same collision.*
  - *Collateral load:* the fan-out (~5,571 accounts in 27 min: 5,292 completed / 170 failed / 539 opted out) drove ms-tables-fields-api to *4.5× normal volume* → p95 3.25s → monitor 299251779. tables-fields recovered by 14:00Z (0/180 buckets over threshold).

*Root-cause analysis (queries run this cycle, numbers observed):*
  • `es_search.py search --query 'fields.dd_service.keyword:"app-update-agent" AND messageTemplate.keyword:*App Publish - Started*'` → the 13:13:13.53Z publish event above (only *3* publishes in 7 days).
  • `es_search.py aggregate … AND level.keyword:"Error" AND fields.AppId.keyword:"55b7fa26…" --field fields.Account.keyword --top 400` → *196 distinct accounts*. Job log lines are the complete population — no extrapolation needed.
  • `dd_search.py metric --query 'sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:tables-fields}.as_count()'` 11:00–16:00Z → *today 58,036 / peak 4,182 @13:28Z* vs *07-14 12,817 / peak 802* = *4.5×*.
  • `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:tables-fields}` → peak *3.25s* (median 0.059s, 29 buckets >1s, 13:13→13:41Z); `post_/v1/field/saveviewbundleinternal` p95 peak *10.72s*.

*Three KB entries bare-match on monitor id and all three are WRONG — do not trust them here:*
  • `ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency` (299251779) — *causality inverted*. First bundle failure 13:13:17.21Z; first `Redis Cache Circuit Breaker OPENED` 13:13:27.74Z — *10s later*. All 11 opens sit inside the push window. Redis was the victim of the load, not its cause.
  • `ki-2026-07-06-runtime-core-redis-cache-timeout-transient-burst` (227940275) — *wrong service*. `trace.redis.command.errors by {service}` 13:00–14:00Z = tables-fields *41*, nonprod/apps 6, syncapi 1, *runtime-core-api 0*. That entry is specifically runtime-core `CacheContext`.
  • `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring` (115456700) — real, but *independent* of this push (breached 13:05:25Z, 8 min BEFORE the publish; still breaching 14:51Z while tables-fields was clean). Posted separately as occurrence #238.

*Suggested next action:* file a defect against App Install/Update — (1) make bundle application atomic / roll back `SuccessfulBundle` on partial failure; (2) reconcile the 196 accounts stranded on v181 content + a v182 preference field; (3) throttle the push consumer — v181 did the same at 1/3 scale on 07-08, this grows with the subscriber base; (4) add a monitor on app-update job failure rate — 196 accounts failed and every monitor that fired named the wrong service.

Source alerts (~174 total):
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1784121195616799  (alert-system, 13:13 UTC — first failure)
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1784122582751369  (alert-system, 13:36 UTC)
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1784122845376119  (alert-system, 13:40 UTC — data-misaligned variant)
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/C09D5KJRBSS/p1784121583732879  (alert-no-code-next-gen, 13:19 UTC — tables-fields p95)

Evidence:
  • DD monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299251779 — "tables-fields high p95" (collateral) · https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/227940275 — "Redis Errors is High" (collateral) · https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700 — "RTC Screen Load" (independent)
  • Kibana — app-update-agent errors (530 hits, verified non-empty): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-07-15T13:13:00Z',to:'2026-07-15T13:50:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword%3A%22app-update-agent%22%20AND%20level.keyword%3A%22Error%22'))
  • Kibana — tables-fields errors (287 hits, verified non-empty): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-07-15T13:13:00Z',to:'2026-07-15T13:50:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword%3A%22tables-fields%22%20AND%20level.keyword%3A%22Error%22'))
  • DD logs — app-update-agent errors: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aapp-update-agent%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1784121180000&to_ts=1784123400000&live=false
  • DD APM — slow bundle saves: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Atables-fields%20%40duration%3A%3E1s&start=1784121180000&end=1784123400000
  • This-window concentration: app-update-agent 542 errors | tables-fields 287 | runtime-core-api 98
  • Investigation: `docs/investigations/2026-07-15-2bc49da0e23cdcf0.md` · KB: `ki-2026-07-15-app-update-push-salesorders-v182-name-collision`

_Caveat: account_impact.py could not resolve any affected account (clusters prod3–5 unconfigured), so impact is stated as 196 named accounts, not active users — a tooling gap, not a finding of zero impact. Why those 196 collide and the other ~5,375 don't is not yet established; it needs a tenant-DB read._

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #238.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`)
Playbook: confirm the pattern via the APM p95 series; latency-only, no error logs by design — do NOT build a Kibana log link for this entry.
Open Jira: none (fix_status: investigating)

*Posting because the 24h suppression window lapsed* (last notified 2026-07-13T18:40Z).

*Why this is NOT part of today's app-update incident* (the interesting bit): monitor 115456700 triggered at *13:05:25Z — 8 minutes BEFORE* the 13:13:13Z App Publish that caused everything else this morning, and it was *still* breaching at 14:51Z (12/180 buckets >3s, peak 8.50s) while tables-fields had fully recovered (0/180 buckets >1s). Ordering and independence both check out — this is the chronic signal, not blast radius.

*Root-cause analysis (run this cycle):*
  • `dd_search.py metric --query 'p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}'` 13:00–15:00Z → *11 points over the 3s threshold*, peak *10.72s @13:45Z*, median 1.13s.
  • 14:00–15:00Z (after the push ended): *12/180 buckets >3s, peak 8.50s* — still elevated with tables-fields clean, which is what rules out a shared cause.
  • Fires observed today: 13:05:25Z (5.59s), 13:48:23Z, 14:52:23Z (3.249s) — all self-recovered.

Source alerts:

  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1784127143207939  (14:52 UTC — after the push, tables-fields healthy)

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 4)
Channel: alert-system (synthetic, degraded-cycle DD monitor scan)  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 3
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Growth` (`@growth` / `#team-growth`)

Symptoms:
  - Service Signup high error rate (154230536, 14:45:56Z)
  - Service Signup Availability SLO in Alert state — 7-day error budget >30% (154229727, 14:46:27Z)
  - Service Signup unexpected number of errors (154163500, 14:53:40Z)

Trace IDs: 6a579cef000000007fbfa80d59faed22, 6a579be700000000de11187626bccb55
Likely cause: single anonymous user's Microsoft-SSO signup session — "Grants retrieval failed - Unauthorized" (invalid code) on the OAuth callback, immediately followed by a missing anti-forgery cookie (__RequestVerificationToken) error on the follow-up POST /Initiate. Same IP/browser both times. Plausible SameSite-cookie-vs-cross-site-OAuth-redirect mechanism; not code-confirmed (method-signup-ui repo fetch blocked, methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 gap).
Suggested next action: file defect — have Growth check method-signup-ui's anti-forgery cookie SameSite policy against external OAuth provider redirects; monitor for recurrence before writing a dedicated KB entry.

  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/154229727  (alert-system, 14:46 UTC)
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/154163500  (alert-system, 14:53 UTC)

Evidence:
  • DD monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/154230536 — "Service Signup has a high error rate on env:prod" (OK, self-recovered)
  • DD monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/154229727 — "Service Signup Availability SLO" (Alert)
  • ES: fields.dd_service.keyword:signup AND level.keyword:Error, 14:00-15:14Z — 2 hits (Grants retrieval failed / HttpAntiForgeryException), same session
  • Note: these 3 monitors co-fired together once before, 2026-07-06, as part of the SQL c2/c3/c4 cascade (alert_hash 112facdd365346cc) — that event is now outside the 7-day SLO window, so today's Alert reflects fresh budget consumption, not a residual echo.
